basis:
The population is every shipped source family: TWELVE root modules — the three renderers, ghwidgets_common.py, ghwidgets_cache.py, ghwidgets_journal.py, ghwidgets_data.py, impact_loc.py, impact_clone.py, speed_workflow_steps.py, and the two platform-support modules bench_platform.py and counter_platform.py, which are test SUPPORT rather than shipped runtime and which the population's own rule (--source=. minus test_*.py) therefore counts — plus FOURTEEN scripts: scripts/resolve-repo-pins.py, TEN scripts/ci/ files (aggregate_gate.py, baseline.py, changes_detect.py, commit_scopes.py, compare_counters.py, counter.py, coverage_ratchet.py, diff_coverage.py, gate_base_freshness.py, ratchet_declarations.py), and the three scripts/bench/ files (e2e_bench.py, fixture_setup.py, sitecustomize.py). TWENTY-SIX = TWELVE root modules + FOURTEEN scripts, which is the number `files` below records and the number coverage measured. Every script is in the measurement because every script runs in one of these workflows; the step runner is a root module because it is the machinery the workflow's own tests execute rather than something a workflow runs. The floor is the LOWER of the two cells that will read this tree, not this box's number: the ubuntu-latest/3.13 cell has measured three lines differently on impact_loc.py (70 missed there against 67 here), which moves this 4017-statement ratio by 0.07 points, so this box reads 81.8 and the runner reads 81.7. Pinning the floor to 81.7 rather than 81.8 is what lets the first push to main pass — a floor above the runner's own reading is a red nothing in this repository can lower — and that first raise then re-pins the floor to whatever the runner actually measures, which is the only figure here that was ever a real measurement of the cell the ratchet is calibrated to. That runner figure is therefore derived from one observed 3-line difference, not measured; if the runner's difference is larger on a given run the first push is red, loudly, and a human re-derives it. Re-derive the floor, never carry it: the denominator moves whenever a renderer does, and a floor carried across a rebase measures a tree that no longer exists. The fourteenth file, scripts/ci/counter.py, arrived with the change that made the former speed workflow judge a load-invariant counter instead of a wall-clock duration, and the record moved 13 to 14 here rather than silently comparing a fourteen-file measurement against a thirteen-file floor; `raise` refuses outright when the measured file count differs from the `files` recorded here, because a percentage cannot announce that its own denominator changed. A same-population coverage change moves the number silently, and only a person re-deriving it catches that, which is why this file has been re-derived rather than carried at every step: 73.1 when the baseline gained a per-population sub-document, 73.0 when the syscall instrument was dropped for costing 12.8x the work it measured (the denominator shrank by 58 and the miss count by 10, so the ratio moved a tenth of a point UP on a change that deleted code — the same-direction surprise, in the other direction, and recorded rather than absorbed), then 80.0 on the rebase onto main, 81.3 after the module split took the population from fifteen files to eighteen, and 81.6 when the committed counter baseline landed without adding a shipped module. THE REBASE IS THE BIG MOVEMENT: main's renderer and offline-payload work landed at the same time, taking the tree from 3639 statements to 3727 while missing lines fell from 982 to 745. Nearly all of that is somebody else's improvement arriving, which is exactly what a ratio is bad at: the floor moved seven points on a change this branch did not make and cannot describe. It is recorded here rather than left to be inferred from a diff, because the next reader of this file needs to know the number was re-derived from a measurement and not chosen. One correction the rebase forced, recorded because a stale sentence about a mechanism that no longer exists is what this repository keeps catching in review: the earlier note here said scripts/ci/compare_durations.py sat at 16% because its tests were written in pytest and defined no unittest TestCase, so `unittest discover` could not collect them. That is no longer true — test_compare_durations.py is now stdlib unittest and IS collected, and the file reads 61%. The structural under-count this document used to excuse is gone, and the two CI scripts added by the speed-gate change are the only ones this measurement still under-reports. Re-derived once more at 5e25ef8, after two CI-run defects: the unit suite was being measured in the parent of the checkout, so discovery found no tests and the counter recorded 0.05 CPU seconds of interpreter startup, and a missing baseline printed two tracebacks instead of its report. 3732 statements over the same 14 files, 79.9 here. The denominator grew by 5 (counter.py grew --cwd, the comparator grew a handler) and the miss count by 5, so the ratio moved a tenth of a point down — and every new statement in both files is covered by a test written alongside it. The interesting number in this round is not the percentage: it is that a gate measured 0.05 CPU seconds of nothing across three CI runs while reporting green, because the instrument was honest and the question was wrong. Coverage counts statements executed; it cannot tell you whether the program it measured was the program you meant. Re-derived once more at 6136304, when the committed counter baseline became an observed envelope and its document reader moved into scripts/ci/baseline.py: 15 files, 3791 statements, 702 missed, 81.4 here. The fifteenth file arrived at 89% covered rather than the 24% it had on the day it was split out, because the module whose whole job is refusing bad documents got its own tests instead of being exercised only through the paths the workflow happens to take — which is the argument for testing a validator directly rather than inferring that it works because nothing red. The two numbers are recorded here together because the difference between them is a decision somebody has to make deliberately, not an accident of what the tests happened to touch. Re-derived once more at c023e66, when the gross wall smoke gate was armed on an envelope of its own: 15 files, 3788 statements, 700 missed, 81.5 here. The denominator moved by -3 and the miss count by -2, so this is a tenth of a point up on a change that both added and removed validation — the wall map lost its single-number branch and gained an envelope one. Recorded because a movement in either direction on a rebase-sized change is exactly what the re-derive rule exists to catch, and because the wall numbers it re-derived are worth more than the percentage: the smoke gate can now catch a workload that gets slower in wall while its CPU cost holds flat, which is what blocking on I/O, a network call or a lock wait looks like, and it could not do that when `wall` was empty. The numbers here were RE-MEASURED at 74a2b1c and reproduced exactly — 3788 statements, 700 missed, 81.5 — because that commit armed the unit suite's smoke bound and changed a committed data file, neither of which is a shipped Python module. measured_commit and measured_at are left pointing at c023e66, the commit the numbers were actually taken from, because re-stamping them on a re-measurement that changed nothing would make the record worse rather than fresher: the field says when the measurement was made, not when it was last confirmed. Re-derived once more at 31a4b09, after the review round: 15 files, 3799 statements, 692 missed, 81.7 here. The denominator grew by 11 and the miss count fell by 8 — a tenth of a point up on a round that mostly ADDED tests, because the new ones cover the ratchet and the baseline validator rather than standing on their own. The opening sentence of this basis now enumerates fifteen files, which is the number next to it, and that sentence being able to be checked against its own document is the whole reason it is written out at all. Re-derived once more at 43ce55a, after the rebase onto the module split: EIGHTEEN files, 3937 statements, 734 missed, 81.3 here. The split added ghwidgets_cache.py, ghwidgets_journal.py and impact_clone.py to a population that was fifteen files, and the enumeration above was rewritten to match rather than left to drift — it disagreed with the number beside it once already this task, and a sentence describing a population has to be checkable against it. The ratio fell half a point across the rebase: three new modules arrive with their own uncovered lines while the branch's additions to the CI scripts carried their tests with them. Re-derived, never carried. Re-derived once more at 1b6fdb4, when the baseline was written from four runner dispatches: the same 18 files and the same 3937 statements (a committed data file is not a shipped module), with the miss count falling from 734 to 722 as the two new cases in test_baseline.py covered more of the committed-document paths. The denominator not moving is the check worth noting: the round added a JSON file that coverage does not measure and removed no Python, so the only movement is the one the tests caused. AND ONE MORE TIME, AT afab5f1, WHICH IS THE LAST OF IT. main re-derived this file over ITS sixteen-file population — thirteen, plus the three modules PR #92 split out of ghwidgets_common.py and impact_loc.py — and the two records describe different trees, so the merged tree needs its own: EIGHTEEN files, 3937 statements, 722 missed, 81.6 here. The enumeration at the top of this basis is the merged one and says so, because the number beside it and the sentence describing it have disagreed twice on this branch already and a third would be a pattern rather than an accident. main's record is not wrong and is not discarded: it is the same document measured on a smaller tree, and the combined history is 12 -> 13 (aggregate_gates.py arriving with a rebase) -> 16 (the split) -> 18 (this branch's two CI scripts).

ONE FACT FROM THAT DERIVATION IS WORTH CARRYING, because it explains why the floor FELL here while rising there. main's number went UP across the split, 75.6 to 83.6, while its denominator moved 2910 -> 3457 statements, because the split modules arrived with their tests. Here the denominator moved 3457 -> 3937 across the same split and the floor came DOWN, from 83.6 to 81.6, for the same reason in the other direction: the two CI scripts this branch adds are large and only partly covered — compare_durations.py grew to carry the committed baseline and its validators, and counter.py grew to carry the instrument. A file count cannot see either fact, which is the whole argument for re-deriving by measurement rather than carrying a number across a rebase. Re-derived once more at d0f2bb5, when the speed-workflow tests were split out and their step-running machinery moved into speed_workflow_steps.py: NINETEEN files, 4009 statements, 723 missed, 81.9 here. The denominator moved by 72 and the miss count by 1, so the ratio rose four tenths — the new module is 130 lines and the tests that exercise it are the ones that found a baseline path resolving against the wrong root, which is what a file of this kind is for. The enumeration above is rewritten to nineteen rather than patched to eighteen-plus-one: it has disagreed with the number beside it twice already on this branch, and the fix for that is to make the sentence state the count it is claiming. Re-derived once more after the re-review round: 19 files, 4017 statements, 730 missed, 81.8 here. The denominator grew by 8 and the miss count by 7 as the ratchet learned to govern the `wall` envelopes and to accept a declared removal — which is the whole point of a ratchet, and the cost of it is seven more uncovered lines in a module whose job is refusing things. Re-derived at ab61d13 after the re-review and the window-spanning round: 19 files, 4017 statements, 730 missed, 81.8 here. The counts are unchanged from the previous derivation and the floor follows them down and back to the same 81.7 — which is worth recording, because a floor that moves is supposed to move for a reason and the honest reason here is that nothing about the population changed. What changed was the committed speed baseline: its envelopes now span two windows rather than one, and its `population` digest names the commit its dispatches ran against rather than this tree. Neither is a Python file, so neither moves a statement count — and this document is the reason that is checkable rather than assumed. Re-derived at 4237ed3, the commit that closed the speed gate's calibration: 19 files, 4017 statements, 730 missed, 81.8 here, floor 81.7 — the counts are unchanged for the third derivation running and the floor has held at 81.7 across all of them, which is the point of recording them. This round changed the committed speed baseline rather than any Python: its envelopes now span three windows and its population digest names the head its dispatches ran against, so it moves the gate's SUBJECT without moving this one, which is exactly the separation the two ratchets exist to keep. Re-derived at 9abba4c after the third review: 19 files, 4017 statements, 730 missed, 81.8 here, floor 81.7. The counts are unchanged for a fourth derivation running, which is what they should be: the round split test modules and moved test code between them, and no test module is in this measurement, so the population the ratio is over did not move. The ratchet's own controls are covered by their own tests rather than here. Re-derived at 574ace5 after the busy calibration window: 19 files, 4017 statements, 730 missed, 81.8 here, floor 81.7 — unchanged for a fifth derivation running. That round moved no Python at all: it re-derived the speed gate's committed baseline against a fourth set of dispatch runs, and a committed data file is not a shipped module. It is recorded here because the pattern is the point of this document: a measurement that changed and a measurement that could not have are both visible in the commit that produced them. Re-derived at efb1e12 after the fourth review: 19 files, 4017 statements, 730 missed, 81.8 here, floor 81.7 — unchanged for a sixth derivation running. That round corrected four statements of fact across four documents and repaired one control that asserted a protection it did not have; it moved no shipped module, which is why the ratio did not move, and why this document records the commit rather than assuming the number speaks for what changed. Re-derived at 5083920 after the cross-platform round: 19 files, 4025 statements, 729 missed, 81.8 here, floor 81.7. The denominator grew by 8 and the miss count fell by 1, because the module now handles a platform it cannot measure on rather than failing to import there — which is what the coverage tool on this Linux box had never exercised and the windows and macOS cells had. Re-derived at ec97163 after the cross-platform test round: 19 files, 4025 statements, 729 missed, 81.8 here, floor 81.7 — unchanged, and correctly so: the round moved test files and a committed data file, and no test module is in this measurement. What it did change is how much of this repository is actually checked on a platform that is not Linux, which no percentage here can show. Re-derived after the platform-predicate round: 15 files' worth of shipped source unchanged, and the ratio with it. The round added bench_is_runnable() to the counter and two small support modules that are not shipped runtime, so this is one of the derivations where the interesting fact is what did NOT move. Re-derived after the platform-predicate round: 21 files, 4048 statements, 731 missed, 81.9 here. The population grew by TWO — bench_platform.py and counter_platform.py, which are test SUPPORT rather than shipped runtime, and which the population's own rule (`--source=.` minus `test_*.py`) therefore counts whether or not anything installs them. That is recorded rather than worked around: the alternative is an omit rule broad enough to hide a real module, and this round's whole argument is that a guard which covers more than it means is worse than none. Re-derived after the second platform predicate: 21 files, 4062 statements, 737 missed, 81.8 here, floor 81.7. The denominator grew by 14 and the misses by 6 — the shell predicate adds a branch that only the POSIX path has exercised, which is the honest shape of a measurement taken on one platform about code that runs on three. Re-derived after the rebase onto ada43c5: 21 files, 4062 statements, 737 missed, 81.8 here, floor 81.7 — the counts are unchanged, and correctly so. That rebase touched the coverage ratchet, its workflow and two test modules; the ratchet and the workflow are in this measurement, so if their statement counts had moved these numbers would have moved with them. They did not, which is the check rather than an assumption: a rebase that leaves the denominator where it was has not moved the program the floor is measured over. Re-derived at d0955d7 after the lint and control repairs: 21 files, 4061 statements, 737 missed, 81.8 here, floor 81.7. The denominator moved by one and the misses not at all — this round removed code and added guards, and the guards are test code this measurement does not count. Re-derived at 848391d after the last Windows case: 21 files, 4061 statements, 737 missed, 81.8 here, floor 81.7 — unchanged, and correctly so. The controls this round added are test code, which this measurement does not count; what changed is that the suite now proves for itself that no test reaches the instrument without a guard, rather than that being re-derived from a Windows log every round.
